SHA-256 of the news article set actually used
run.fingerprint_note: Two runs with the same fingerprint produced the same outputs. A different fingerprint means an input, a module or an assumption moved, and the results are not comparable without saying so.

code.note: Hashed so a change to any module invalidates comparability.

assumptions.name: TOP_K
assumptions.controls: How many names each factor sleeve nominates each month.
assumptions.risk_if_wrong: Tied to the 5% position cap: N names at 5% can place N*5% of capital. Below 20 names the book cannot be fully invested.

assumptions.name: TX_COST
assumptions.controls: Cost on the factor-level dynamic strategy only.
assumptions.risk_if_wrong: The stock-level book uses COST_BPS instead; this one does not affect the authoritative result.

assumptions.name: COST_BPS
assumptions.controls: Base round-trip cost on traded notional for the stock-level book.
assumptions.risk_if_wrong: A full sensitivity ladder is reported at 0/10/20/50/100 bps, so the conclusion does not rest on this value.

assumptions.name: REGIME_MIN_TRAIN_MONTHS
assumptions.controls: Warm-up before the regime model is allowed to score out of sample.
assumptions.risk_if_wrong: Lowering it lets the mixture be fitted and scored on months it has already seen, which reintroduces look-ahead.

assumptions.name: REGIME_MODEL_VERSION
assumptions.controls: Identifies the regime model configuration used.
assumptions.risk_if_wrong: A label only; the parameters live in regime_model.py.

assumptions.name: WINSOR_TAIL
assumptions.controls: Percentile clip applied to each raw metric before scaling.
assumptions.risk_if_wrong: Too small leaves outliers able to dominate a cross-sectional rank; too large erases genuine signal at the extremes.

assumptions.name: MIN_METRIC_COVERAGE
assumptions.controls: Share of composite metric weight that must be present for a factor score to be produced at all.
assumptions.risk_if_wrong: Below this threshold a score is withheld rather than computed from whatever metrics survived.

assumptions.name: MIN_SECTOR_SIZE
assumptions.controls: Smallest sector that is demeaned; smaller ones keep raw values.
assumptions.risk_if_wrong: Demeaning a group of two against its own mean would drive both to zero and discard real signal.

assumptions.name: CONSTRAINTS
assumptions.controls: Hard limits the allocator must satisfy in every month.
assumptions.risk_if_wrong: A breach would mean the reported backtest held positions the stated construction could not have built.

assumptions.name: RISK_FREE_ANNUAL
assumptions.controls: Risk-free rate used for the excess-return Sharpe and Jensen's alpha. Not measured: the source data has no G-Sec series.
assumptions.risk_if_wrong: Moves Sharpe from 1.41 (at zero) to 1.07. Both are reported, so no conclusion depends on the exact value.

assumptions.name: CI_LEVEL
assumptions.controls: Width of the bootstrap confidence intervals.
assumptions.risk_if_wrong: A narrower interval would overstate precision.

assumptions.name: BOOTSTRAP_SEED
assumptions.risk_if_wrong: Unpinned, the interval would change on every run and could not be quoted as a result.

assumptions.name: BOOTSTRAP_SAMPLES
assumptions.risk_if_wrong: Too few resamples makes the interval itself noisy, which is a different kind of uncertainty from the one being measured.

data_freshness.trading_calendar_note: Weekends and fixed-date NSE closures are excluded. Diwali and other lunar holidays are not modelled, so a genuine holiday may be counted as a missed trading day. The count errs conservative.

issues.detail: EOD data stops at 2026-09-29, one trading day behind 2026-09-29. Usually the refresh has not run yet today.

Monthly tables are labelled through 2026-09-30 but the newest close in the database is 2026-09-29, a gap of 1 days. Months are keyed by calendar month-end, so an in-progress month always carries a future date. The label is a bucket, not a claim that trading reached it -- but nothing in the table says so.
The last refresh that actually delivered data resolved 2026-09-29. Attempts since then have not extended the series.

recent_refresh_runs.latest_message: Inserted/updated real NSE EOD rows from https://nsearchives.nseindia.com/products/content/sec_bhavdata_full_29092026.csv

determinism.basis: k-means++ init is seeded inside regime_model; components are aligned across refits with linear_sum_assignment, so component order cannot drift between months.
Pure cross-sectional arithmetic. No sampling, no fitting.
Bounded water-filling on a fixed input, no randomness.

Compounds a fixed weight path. Cost enters linearly. Weights are summed in sorted order: iterating a set of tickers follows Python's per-process hash randomisation and float addition is not associative, which produced ~1e-6 run-to-run drift in turnover before it was fixed.
random.Random(seed) with a fixed seed, so the interval is identical on every run.

Fetched live from RSS this run, so the article set depends on the network. A difference here moves the current month's news sentiment, then news_stress_score, then transition_risk, then the regime row, the allocation and the rebalance trades. Measured across two runs it perturbed 1 month of 153 and changed no regime label -- small, but not reproducible. The article set was snapshotted and hashed into the fingerprint, so this run can still be replayed exactly with NEWS_REPLAY=1.

caveats.statement: Partly corrected, and the remainder is now measured rather than asserted. Every month-end of the NSE bhavcopy archive (2019-09 to 2026-08, 84 snapshots) lists every symbol that traded that day, so the trading universe is known directly. A symbol is now scored only in months it had already started trading, which removes 36 of 189 database symbols from the 56% of backtest months the archive covers -- several were 2024-25 listings previously carried back to 2014. The gate is worth 0.6pp of CAGR and 1.1pp of drawdown. What remains is exclusion rather than look-forward: 412 symbols traded at the start of the archive and had stopped by the end, and the database holds none of them, against a trading universe that grew from 1699 to 3232 names. Those are invisible to today's Nifty 200 list, so the return remains biased upward by an unknown amount.
caveats.why_not_fixed: Correcting the remaining 412 names needs fundamentals for tickers never ingested, which is paid data acquisition rather than calculation. The archive also only reaches 2019-09, so the 68 earlier backtest months are ungated.

caveats.statement: 16 of 189 symbols (8%) are structurally invisible to the Value and Quality factors. They are all in Financial Services: a bank has no revenue line to grow and deposits are not debt in the sense debt/equity assumes. 10,970 factor score-months are withheld, and this is the largest single cause -- not missing data, but a sector whose reporting conventions do not map onto the metrics. Momentum and Low Volatility are price-based and still cover these names.
caveats.why_not_fixed: Fixing it needs bank-specific metrics (NIM, GNPA, NPA ratio, PCR, CASA) sourced from filings, and equity metrics that are comparable across the two sector types. Adding them is a data acquisition project, not a calculation change.

caveats.statement: 2 symbols (SWIGGY, VMM) have fundamental rows but no populated metric in any month. Unlike the banks, this is an ingestion gap rather than an economic fact, and it is probably a recent listing with no extracted history.
caveats.why_not_fixed: Upstream extraction. The coverage rule correctly withholds their scores rather than guessing from partial data.

caveats.statement: 6 symbols carry metrics in fewer than half their months, so the coverage rule withholds their score in most months and they contribute unevenly to the factors: BAJFINANCE (50% of 149 months), HYUNDAI (9% of 22 months), M&MFIN (49% of 149 months), PREMIERENE (14% of 22 months), SHRIRAMFIN (48% of 149 months), WAAREEENER (9% of 22 months). The rule is doing the conservative thing here, since a score computed from the months that happen to be populated would be noisier than no score at all.
caveats.why_not_fixed: The missing months are absent upstream, not dropped downstream -- the rows exist in fundamentals_monthly and the metric columns are empty. Fixing it means re-extracting the filing history for these tickers. The pipeline already handles the consequence correctly by withholding rather than imputing, so this affects breadth of coverage rather than correctness of what is reported.

caveats.statement: Sharpe is computed against the measured Indian 10-year G-Sec yield from macro_monthly, averaging 7.19% over the window and spanning 5.98% to 8.73%. It is applied month by month, not as a single average. One caveat remains: the series is a yield, so it is a contemporaneous rate rather than a return actually earned in that month, which slightly overstates the excess return in a risk-off period when yields fall alongside prices.
caveats.why_not_fixed: A realised total-return index on 10-year G-Secs would be the correct benchmark, and no such series is in the database.

caveats.statement: The 26.58% CAGR point estimate has a 95% interval of 12.83% to 40.34%. The interval is roughly 28 points wide: 149 monthly returns cannot pin down a growth rate more precisely than that. The window analysis says how much of that is spread: of 114 overlapping 36-month stretches, 114 compounded positively (100.0%), with a median of 25.0% and a range of 0.1% to 55.8%. The worst was 2017-04 to 2020-03, the best 2022-07 to 2025-06. A reader starting at an arbitrary date would have experienced the median, not the headline.
caveats.why_not_fixed: A longer out-of-sample history would narrow it, and no amount of statistics manufactures months that did not happen. The rolling windows narrow the practical uncertainty without pretending the sample grew.

caveats.statement: The reported Sharpe of 1.007 is the best of 16 effectively independent configurations, not one chosen in advance. Against the 0.7499 that the best of that many random strategies would be expected to reach, a strategy this strong appears by chance roughly 27% of the time. The deflated figure is 0.2571. A simulation-calibrated bar, which is less strict, would give 0.4821.
caveats.why_not_fixed: This is not a defect in the calculation; it is what the sample supports. Closing the gap needs either more out-of-sample history, a strategy fixed in advance rather than selected, or a fresh sample the search never touched.

caveats.statement: Beta of 0.985 looks market-neutral, but R-squared of 79% means 79% of monthly variance is still the index's. The alpha is real; the diversification benefit is not.
caveats.why_not_fixed: Tested, and the obvious remedy does not work. Re-running the allocator with the sector cap tightened from 30% to 8% left R-squared at 76-79% the whole way while beta fell 1.04 to 0.75 and CAGR fell 29.6% to 20.7%. Sector concentration is not the cause; the correlation is what a long-only equity book is. Lowering it needs shorting or hedging the index, which is a different strategy rather than a fix to this one.

caveats.statement: Average of the worst 5% of months is -10.2%, the worst single month was -20.9%, and the book spent 24 consecutive months below a prior peak. A mean and a Sharpe ratio both hide this.
caveats.why_not_fixed: Inherent to a long-only equity book. Disclosed rather than smoothed away.

caveats.statement: 60 of 153 months carry no regime score, because the mixture refuses to fit and score a month before its warm-up ends. Those months are labelled 'Unscored' and the allocator holds an explicitly neutral 0.5 confidence rather than a fabricated one. The regime input is therefore absent for the first 60 months of the backtest, which is roughly 39% of the period.
caveats.why_not_fixed: A shorter warm-up would let the mixture be fitted and scored on months it has already seen, which is precisely the look-ahead the warm-up exists to prevent.
caveats.provenance_check: No warm-up month is labelled with the GMM model version, so the output does not claim a provenance it does not have.

caveats.statement: News features are populated for 61 of 153 months (40% coverage, 56 inside the backtest window, 405.0 articles in total), at a mean confidence of about 0.08. A feature absent in more than half the months is not measuring sentiment; it is partly measuring article availability.
caveats.why_not_fixed: The archive only goes back so far. This is why the news factor is weighted by its own confidence rather than treated as a full-strength input, and why it is retained as decision context rather than removed outright.

caveats.statement: No supervised learning layer is fitted. A learner needs substantially more forward return periods than exist here before it can be validated out of sample, and fitting one on this data would be overfitting dressed as sophistication.
caveats.why_not_fixed: Requires more out-of-sample history, not a different algorithm.
